newsitem.title: USA: Ill. House rep wants gambling to fund school bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ill. House rep wants gambling to fund school bonds.

text.p: A state representative on Monday proposed expanded gambling in Illinois that would partly fund $10 billion of bonds for school construction and nearly $800 million in property tax relief.

State Rep. Lou Lang, D-Skokie, estimated that expanded gambling could generate up to $1.4 billion in new revenues to support issuing $1 billion of school construction bonds for each of the next five years.
The construction bonds would be matched with local funds, producing the $10 billion figure, Lang, a strong proponent of gaming, stated in a news release.
But based on the reports he has received, Gov. Jim Edgar would not approve the proposal if it got to him and he does not expect it to get to him, spokesman Mike Lawrence said.
"Please don't ask me to analyze why Lou Lang is doing this, he and I aren't on the same wavelength," Lawrence said.
Edgar is "not at all excited about expanding gambling in Illinois," Lawrence said.

Edgar has said previously that he would consider a proposal to allow riverboat gambling in Cook County, which was specifically excluded by Illinois legislators when they first approved gaming, Lawrence added.

Lang proposes to authorize land-based casinos in Chicago, allow dockside gaming aboard the state's riverboats and restructure the gaming tax rates. The legislation also would allow slot machines at race tracks and allocate 41 percent of their proceeds to horse racing purses.
